headline: unit+9D4h is the plane's squadron, not a pilot control block. The pilot control block is unit+9E4h: five float axes and three bytes, latched into unit+BB0h each step by 007B9770.

The flight controller is the object at unit+AB0h, constructed by 007D7EA0(this, unit) from the plane unit constructor 007CFD20 at 007CFF87; it holds the unit at +8h and the plane class descriptor (unit+538h) at +0Ch.

The per-step law is the tick element's slot +8h, 007CE040, shared by all five plane classes; its motion dispatch at 007CEC30-007CECB4 picks one of three arms, and the free-flight arm reaches the core law through 007CC2F0 -> 007DC830 -> 007DB680 -> 007DA710.
The Dynamics/* tuning group is mirrored verbatim from tuning+210h to 00F872F0 by a single REP MOVSD at 007EAAE1, which is why the flight code reads absolute globals instead of calling 0042E740.

corrections.was: the tasks write "the pilot control block at unit+9D4h", with a desired cruising altitude at +394h, a second altitude at +398h, a third value at +39Ch and a dirty flag at +3ADh
corrections.is: unit+9D4h is the plane's squadron. Those four fields are squadron fields: a formation-level cruising altitude and its limits. The pilot control block is unit+9E4h, five float axes and three bytes.
corrections.evidence: scanning .text for every MOV [reg+9D4h] gives ten stores. 007ED0E6 in 007ED0D0 writes plane+9D4h = squadron together with plane+9D8h = spawnIndex and the sorted insert into squadron+3D0h[]; 007F4B49 does the same in 007F4580; 007F3A07 clears it in BSP_Squadron_RemovePlane; 007CFE6C zeroes it in the plane unit constructor. 009FBA50 at 009FBA90 reads approach+0Ch (= unit+9D4h) and then +394h as a shared altitude ceiling. The existing readers agree: [[unit+9D4h]+3D0h] == unit (docs/HUD_CENTRAL_UPDATES.md), [unit+9D4h]+3CCh (docs/MISSION_RESULT_DECISION.md), 007B97E0 MOV EAX,[ECX+9D4h]; RET (docs/GUNNERY_TABLES.md).
